text.p: Champion Enterprises Inc said Wednesday it expects full-year 1997 earnings of $1.62 to $1.67 a share.
The projection assumes that the housing industry grows four to seven percent this year and the economy continues to be strong, said Champion, a manufactured housing company.

"We remain committed to our three-year goal of increasing earnings per share at a compound annual growth rate of 20 percent, with 1995 as the base year and excluding non-recurring charges," Walter Young Jr, chairman, said in a statement.

Champion today reported first quarter net income of $0.28 a share, flat with a year ago. The year-ago results were restated to include Redman Industries Inc, which merged with Champion in October 1996.
First quarter net sales gained 11 percent to $378.9 million from $342.8 million a year ago. Housing sales rose to $363.0 million from $328.6 million.
"Champion's housing revenues and homes sold increased 10 percent for the quarter, primarily due to our 1996 acquisitions and slightly higher volume," Young said.
Champion sold 14,247 homes, up from 12,962 a year ago.

Housing operating margins for the first quarter were 6.2 percent of sales, down from 6.7 percent a year ago. Young said quarterly earnings were hurt by restructuring of the product line at Redman's Indiana facilities and by start-up expenses at three plants.
He also said inclement weather slowed sales and home placements, resulting in higher inventory levels.

As of March 29, unfilled housing orders were about $55 million, down from $64 million at the end of March 1996. The decline was due to increased capacity, with incoming order rates comparable to last year, the company said.

"We believe increased retail sales are not reflected in year-to-date industry shipments, which declined 3.2 percent through February," Young said. "Due to high levels of unfilled orders last year, dealers ordered homes early to assure timely delivery. Currently, dealers appear to be selling from inventory, the levels of which have increased because of the effects of inclement weather."
He said it is possible Champion may be affected by dealer inventories in the second quarter.
